rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 6 "What you can test and check sets your complexity ceiling", line 49: "The plan read is a calibration move." 'The plan read' is not a term used verbatim earlier, but it composes two terms the deck already named: 'read' as the human's own review activity (chunk 4 line 33 "Your read and the agent's walk-down catch different misses"; chunk 5 line 41 "Aim the read at the unknown that teaches you the most") and 'the plan' (used throughout chunks 2-5). By chunk 6 a sequential reader has held both halves across the two immediately preceding slides, so the compound resolves rather than strands. Also checked: 'the agent's walk-down' (chunk 4 line 33) is defined in the same bullet it's used in ("it can keep walking branches without getting bored") — same-chunk, not a forward or absent referent. 'the three pressures' (chunk 6 line 50) points back to chunk 3's own header, one slide within normal deck-narration range. Harm the rule guards against (a reader stranded with no candidate antecedent) is absent in every case checked.

grep -inE 'below|above|further down|at the top|see below|earlier (module|lecture)|opening lecture|previous (module|lecture)|the last (lecture|module|exercise)' over body lines 1-53 → 0 hits. grep -inE '\[[^]]+\]\(' (markdown link syntax) over the same range → 0 hits. No chunk names or locates another file by position; the only named practitioner (Dex Horthy, chunk 2 line 20) is a person credit, not a file callback.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Bold count per chunk: chunk 1 = 0, chunk 2 = 5 (checklist-item handles: **A specific file list.** / **An early runnable slice.** / **A verification step** (trimmed to sub-span) / **Named assumptions.** / **A list of non-goals.**), chunk 3 = 3 (**Structure is persuasive.** / **Reasonableness passes for rightness.** / **You already agree with it.**), chunks 4-6 = 0. Chunks 2 and 3 exceed the default ≤1-per-slide budget, but the maintainer block's dated accept-note (L66, 2026-07-09, Antti-directed "go very lightly on the bold") explicitly authorizes exactly this shape on 'the two checklist slides' by name, matching all 3 named items on chunk 3 and the 3 named items on chunk 2 that predate the later criteria expansion (the 2 bullets added after, L64, carry bold by the same documented convention). Each handle is ≤5 words (a checklist-item name, explicitly one of the rule's own licensed categories), and every non-checklist slide sits at zero bold, satisfying the budget everywhere the accept-note doesn't apply.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 1's header ('Ask plan mode what changed', line 9) is imperative, not a claim — this is a lecture, so the rule's default would expect a claim. The maintainer block's dated accept-note (L68, 2026-08-25, Antti-directed) explicitly defends this exact header as "a do-move imperative (`check_lectures §4` live-do carve-out)" for the specific reason that the prompt's answer must come from the student's own session. The two law/consolidation headers meet the binding requirement as full declarative claims: chunk 5 'Plan review is a high-leverage gate' (line 36) and chunk 6 'What you can test and check sets your complexity ceiling' (line 43). Chunks 2-4 ('Five things a good plan has' / 'Three pressures that make bad plans look good' / 'Two reads, paired') are catalogue-style headers naming their subject, matching the rule's own 'catalogue entries naming their subject' carve-out. Blocking classification (rule added after the template's explicit partition, principle applied per the compendium's own instruction): a mismatched header grammar costs polish, not comprehension — a reader can still follow an imperative-shaped lecture header — so this rule is non-blocking, same family as rule 6.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all bullets across all 6 chunks against the three classes (doctrine restatement, self-referential design commentary, aphorism kicker). Closest candidate: chunk 6, line 51, "Push reach past what you can check and you have not delegated more. You are checking less." reads kicker-shaped (short, punchy, closes a bullet run) but introduces a genuine new distinction (delegating vs. checking) not stated anywhere earlier in the file or restating the chunk's own header — it earns its slot rather than re-announcing an already-landed point. No self-referential curriculum-design commentary found anywhere (the file never talks about its own pedagogy to the student). No doctrine-restatement instances — the mechanism bullets in chunks 5 and 6 each add new content rather than re-stating a split that already did its work. Blocking classification (rule added after the template's explicit partition, principle applied): a low-value bullet wastes attention but doesn't block comprehension, so non-blocking, same family as rule 7's non-superlative sub-items.
